calls.reason: The packet only shows Cursor raising money with thin, improving gross margins, plus a Stripe note that Gamma is profitable. Neither proves or disproves that every AI startup must keep raising more to pay rising model bills.

Both companies' 2025 net losses top $38B, but mostly from one-off non-cash fair-value charges. Anthropic's operating loss was $8B and OpenAI's cash-adjusted loss about $8B, so the answer depends on which loss measure is meant.

OpenAI held over $73B in cash in March 2026 and Anthropic raised $65B in May. Nothing matches those funds against payment schedules or shows that cheap contract signing is the only reason they have kept up.

Ramp says non-tech sectors are closing the gap in paid AI adoption, but it does not measure how many non-tech firms spend substantial amounts. The evidence is about something adjacent and points both ways.

Ramp's lead economist publicly said 80% of the two labs' enterprise revenue comes from 1% of customers and that it is not getting better. That matches the claim's main point, though the three-year span is not documented.

Meta covered about $31B of quarterly capex from operating cash with slightly positive free cash flow, but it also borrows. One quarter from one buyer does not settle a universal claim about GPU prices shrinking the customer pool.
